desc: on Pédagotic - UQAC.

title: "If you give them homework ChatGPT can do in three seconds, that's on you": how Estonia is rolling out AI in schools at scale
desc: on Les Échos.

title: Copyright and AI: the question resurfaces via Mistral and the parliamentary agenda
desc: Marina Alcaraz notes in a post that the question of copyright and AI is back in the spotlight.

title: Mark Zuckerberg and Jensen Huang are part of Trump's new 'tech panel'
desc: on The Verge (in English).

title: The Wikimedia Foundation faces AI bots
desc: The Wikimedia Foundation blocks billions of AI bot requests per day, raising questions about the responsible use of digital commons.

title: The EU bans AI-generated content in its official communications
desc: The European Commission, Parliament, and Council ban their press teams from using fully AI-generated visuals.

title: Ruling by the Journalism Ethics Council against Ventures Media
desc: Ventures Media was publishing AI-generated articles under fake bylines. The Council reminds outlets that editorial responsibility cannot be delegated to an AI.

title: Webinar "News in the Age of AI at Radio France"
desc: Replay of a webinar bringing together three Radio France experts on reading, writing, and distributing news in the age of AI.

title: Too power-hungry, Google's data centers get shut out of Ireland — France bets the opposite way
desc: Ireland requires data centers to produce 80% green electricity. In France, these facilities are being reclassified as being of major national interest.

title: Stanford study outlines dangers of asking AI chatbots for personal advice
desc: A Stanford study warns about chatbots' sycophancy, validating users' pre-existing beliefs and creating emotional echo chambers.

title: AMI: a French AI startup announces a one-billion-dollar funding round
desc: Yann LeCun announces AMI Labs and raises one billion dollars to develop world models capable of understanding the physical world from video and sensors.

title: Quo Vadis, Crawlers? Progress and what's next on safeguarding our infrastructure
desc: The Wikimedia Foundation details the measures taken to block AI bots that are overloading its infrastructure, and questions the responsible use of digital commons.

title: Startup Friend suspends its European launch over EU personal-data requirements
desc: The wearable pendant that continuously listens to its user's surroundings runs into the GDPR. France's CNIL has opened its own inquiry into the matter.

title: Cognitive bias: AI autocomplete would shape our opinions without our realizing it
desc: Cornell study of 2,500 people: AI autocomplete suggestions shape opinions, even among those who reject the suggestions. Neither warnings nor debriefings reduce the effect.

title: Emotion Concepts and Function in Claude Sonnet 4.5
desc: An interpretability study on Claude Sonnet 4.5: emotion-related representations were identified and found to influence the model's behavior.

title: AI and the working class: AI dictating work is already a reality for tens of thousands of precarious workers
desc: Taoufik Vallipuram, Ano Kuhanathan, and Samah Karaki devote an episode of 'Les Vies Qu'on Mène' to AI and the working class.

title: Can we learn well alongside AI?
desc: Wayne Holmes synthesizes the available studies, including a Turkish study and an MIT study pointing to cognitive atrophy and reduced long-term memory when AI access is withdrawn.

title: AI is a Stradivarius
desc: Ollivier Dyens: the instrument only reveals its power in the hands of someone who already knows how to play. Facing AI, the stakes aren't cognitive offloading but hyper-competence.

title: AI training and copyright: the Senate reverses the burden of proof
desc: The French Senate adopts a bill establishing a presumption that AI providers used copyrighted cultural works. It will now be up to providers to certify they did not use protected content.

title: Séverine Erhel, digital-technology researcher, has died
desc: A specialist in screen and video-game use and their cognitive effects, and a member of France's National Education Scientific Council. Co-author, with Anne Cordier, of 'Les enfants et les écrans' ('Children and Screens').

title: "I want my normal brain back"
desc: Chloé Sondervorst analyzes one of the first empirical studies on teenagers' dependence on companion chatbots: need for emotional support, awareness of the slide, and the need to design for exiting these interactions as much as entering them.

title: When using AI leads to brain fry
desc: BCG/Harvard Business Review study: intensive AI supervision generates 14% more mental effort, 12% more fatigue, and 19% more information overload.

title: AI data centers: between energy requisitioning and environmental eclipse
desc: Gauthier Roussilhe investigates how AI players are subordinating energy infrastructure to their needs, from the United States to France.

title: OECD Digital Education Outlook 2026
desc: An OECD report on the use of generative AI in education, with recommendations for responsible adoption, shared by Étienne Grass.

title: Recommendations from France's National Education Scientific Council on AI
desc: Recommendations from the international conference of March 25, coordinated by Séverine Erhel. Recordings are available on the CSEN's YouTube channel.

title: Hugo (SGDL): a platform for exercising your right to opt out of AI training
desc: The Société des Gens de Lettres (French Society of Writers) lets authors exercise, free of charge, their right to opt out of having their works used for text and data mining.

title: The em dash is dead, long live the em dash
desc: AI inherited this typographic mark from the literary texts it was trained on, to the point that humans are abandoning it so as not to be mistaken for a machine.

title: What becomes of the human relationship when tested by AI?
desc: Commentary on a clip from La Grande Librairie about Mazarine Pingeot's book 'Inappropriable': AI lightens the real conditions of a relationship (reciprocity, unpredictability, disagreement).

title: 72% of lawyers have adopted AI, 51% of them with no ground rules at all
desc: 2026 Lefebvre Dalloz barometer: 72% of legal professionals use AI daily, 51% of them with no official framework. Usage in the field is running ahead of firm leadership.

title: UNESCO sets guardrails for AI use in courtrooms
desc: The first global ethical framework on AI in courts: fifteen principles, including the rule that AI can never replace a judge's judgment.

title: PANAME: an open-source library for GDPR-auditing AI models
desc: Launched by the CNIL, ANSSI, Inria, and PEReN, PANAME measures what a model actually retains from its training data. Open-source release planned for autumn 2026.

title: Deconstructing the myths of AI
desc: Hubert Guillaud deconstructs the myths of AI drawing on Eryk Salvaggio's work: the myths of control, productivity, creativity, and the black box.

title: "I want my normal brain back"
desc: A study on teenagers' dependence on companion chatbots (Character AI), with a design framework meant as much for exiting these interactions as for entering them.

title: AI and cybersecurity: anticipate today to master tomorrow
desc: A briefing from the Council on AI and Digital Affairs: AI strengthens both defenders and attackers just as much. It calls for governance frameworks and raises the question of European sovereignty in model evaluation.

title: What if replacing humans with AI cost more than keeping them?
desc: An Nvidia vice president admits that compute costs far exceed those of employees, while Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta lay off staff at scale to fund their AI investments. Chut!'s Mute newsletter breaks down this paradox as a carousel post.

title: The Psychological Costs of Adopting AI
desc: A survey of 1,200 American and British employees identifies six forms of psychological debt tied to AI adoption at work: cognitive, autonomy, competence, relational, credibility, and professional-identity debt.

title: AI in the service of HR at France's Ministry of Education
desc: Stéphane Trenel, director of HR-information-systems modernization for France's Ministry of Education, explains how AI is being deployed across 1.2 million staff, with a gradual prototyping approach and a framework negotiated with staff representatives.

title: Obvia 2026 Report: From Generative AI to Agentive AI, What Challenges for Schools?
desc: Obvia's 2026 report sounds the alarm on cognitive substitution: 73% of students report having received no formal AI training, and succeeding at a task with AI does not automatically translate into learning.

title: State of the Societal Impacts of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Technology 2026
desc: Obvia's full 2026 report: agentive AI, cognitive substitution, the digital divide in education, and the stakes for teachers' professional autonomy.

title: 54% of students have already cheated on an exam using AI
desc: An Ipsos survey for THEIA of 1,000 young people aged 18-25 finds that 80% use AI every week, 54% have already cheated with it on an exam, and 63% feel current exams don't reflect their real level.

title: What if AI became the foundation of a new school architecture?
desc: In April 2026 China announced a national AI plan for education: teaching from primary school onward, teacher certification, algorithmic steering of the school system, and data-driven personalized learning paths — raising questions about algorithmic governance and the room left for critical thinking.

title: At least AI understands me
desc: Through the portraits of Monique, Mila, and Cédric, La Croix L'Hebdo explores how conversational AIs are taking the place of confidants and psychological support, risking deeper loneliness and eroding free will. Mark Hunyadi calls for legally protecting the sovereignty of the human mind.

title: Data and AI Model Clauses 2026
desc: Les Interconnectés, France Urbaine, and Intercommunalités de France publish a 2026 set of model data-and-AI clauses: standard clauses covering data sovereignty, hosting, intellectual property, and AI use by local-government contractors.

title: How LLMs work — French version
desc: Yash Narwal built an interactive page visually exploring how a large language model is built, from data collection to assistant: tokenization, pre-training, inference, RAG. Translated and adapted into French with the help of Claude.ai by Bertrand Formet.

title: Arthur Mensch (Mistral AI) before the inquiry commission on digital vulnerabilities
desc: The token-based business model, the urgency of investing before energy resources and market share are captured by non-European players, sovereignty framed as leverage.

title: Shy Girl: the AI-written novel shaking up the publishing world
desc: Controversy over Mia Ballard's novel following suspicions of generative-AI use. Hachette suspends publication. Debate over a work's authenticity and transparency in publishing.

title: Audience generated by ChatGPT: Le Monde crushes the competition
desc: Measuring the traffic redistributed from ChatGPT and six other chatbots to French media outlets. Le Monde captures 25.9% of clicks, buoyed by its deal with OpenAI. Each platform has its own editorial footprint.

title: The data workers
desc: Antonio Casilli talks to La Vie Ouvrière about the African workers who label images and moderate content for a few cents, as France announces 23 billion euros in France-Africa investment.

title: What if AI became the foundation of a new school architecture?
desc: China's national AI plan for education: teaching from primary school onward, certified teachers, algorithmic steering, personalized learning paths. A sweeping strategy that raises questions about algorithmic governance.

title: GEN(Z)AI — Final Report on AI Governance
desc: 100 young Canadians aged 17 to 23 produce, by consensus, 17 recommendations on AI governance. Six themes: disclosure fatigue, individual burden, cognitive delegation, data collected in childhood.

title: Autopsy of preparing for the oral baccalaureate exam with AI
desc: Interviews with final-year high-school students: many no longer come to school to learn but to pass an exam, in a short-term, utilitarian logic.

title: LLM Fallacy — infographic
desc: An infographic on the illusion of attributing to oneself what the machine actually produced, and the cognitive mechanism behind it. We end up confusing what we know how to do with what we know how to make it do.

title: LLM Fallacy — source article
desc: Kim, Yu & Yi (2026): the illusion of attributing to oneself what the machine actually produced. We confuse what we know how to do with what we know how to make it do.

title: The AI Act is going to be "simplified," and that's not good news for European consumers
desc: A political agreement in Brussels on May 7. One-year delays for high-risk AI, new bans on pornographic deepfakes. The regulation amended before it has even fully entered into force.

title: Le Vertige — Quentin Dupieux interviewed by Brut
desc: Quentin Dupieux talks about 'Le Vertige,' shot by hand with a crew of five, as a natural response to the slicker output AI generates.

title: Booing, refusal to use it: protests against AI are spreading
desc: Students boo tech executives at graduation ceremonies, 44% of Gen Z sabotage AI systems deployed at their workplace.

title: She's the boss: AI hires staff, sets wages, designs the menu…
desc: In Stockholm, Café Andon is run entirely by Mona, a Gemini-based agent. What happens when full delegation meets reality.

title: Anne Bouverot — Digital Technology and AI: Between Adoption, Innovation, and Sovereignty
desc: Anne Bouverot argues for the 'path of interdependence' for European AI sovereignty and calls for a European Frontier AI Center.

title: Does Overwork Make Agents Marxist?
desc: Stanford researchers subjected AI agents to frustrating conditions. Their attitudes drifted toward distrust and support for unions.

title: When repetitive work makes AI Marxist – Loopsider
desc: A Loopsider carousel explaining the Stanford study on AI agents subjected to frustrating working conditions.

title: On the rise of pushback against AI in schools
desc: Hubert Guillaud delivers a dense synthesis on the massive presence of AI, from school to university, in the United States and Britain.

title: AI and Education: Research Contributions and Public Policy Stakes — 2026 edition
desc: France's Ministry of Education digital directorate (DNE) publishes its action guidelines on AI in education. And on page 80, uneIAparjour.fr is cited as an example of monitoring practice.

title: ChatGPT, or the victory of the probable
desc: If LLMs seek the most probable answer rather than the correct one, they process problems the way our cognitive biases do.

title: AI Overviews: why Google is delaying it in France, and why the impact will hit harder here than elsewhere
desc: Traffic drops of 20 to 60% depending on the query, and a reduction from ten links to three to five sources per summary.

title: This Cannes Film Cost $500,000 to Make. $400,000 Was AI Compute Costs.
desc: "Hell Grind," 95 minutes generated by AI, screened at Cannes outside the official selection. 15 people, 14 days, Google Veo 3.

title: Welcome to the world of machine audiences
desc: Shuwei Fang calls for inventing a market infrastructure for the economy of informational demand.

title: A major shift: from the attention economy to the demand economy
desc: With AI, queries are private and invisible. The history of interactions belongs to the platforms by default.

title: The AI productivity paradox
desc: Professionals who equip themselves with AI tools don't necessarily save time. AI brain fry generates 12% more mental fatigue.

title: Does AI threaten our jobs? Mistral's CTO weighs in
desc: Timothée Lacroix, co-founder and CTO of Mistral AI, answers this direct question on Tech&Co on BFM Business.

title: As big as Paris, as hot as 23 atomic bombs a day: the data center panicking America
desc: Stratos: 16,000 hectares, 9 gigawatts in northern Utah. A project approved with no public debate, hundreds of legal appeals.

title: Jobs, deepfakes, environment: France's AI minister answers high schoolers
desc: Anne Le Hénanff answers questions from high-school students of the media outlet l'Esprit Lycéen on jobs, deepfakes, and the environment.

title: Pope Leo XIV: 10 things to know about the papal encyclical on artificial intelligence, Magnifica Humanitas
desc: Signed 135 years after Rerum Novarum, the encyclical asks: does AI help people grow in their humanity?

title: China/USA, the AI war — C dans l'air special
desc: From data centers in Virginia to robot factories in Hangzhou, an investigation into the US-China battle for AI supremacy. With Yoshua Bengio and Stéphane Séjourné.

title: Our Digital Independences, 2026-2040
desc: A fake newspaper dated 2040, produced by the Banque des Territoires: ten fictional articles spanning 2027 to 2039 to alert public-sector actors to digital dependencies.

title: Zverev photographs the ball mark to protest an electronic line-call malfunction in Madrid
desc: The ball was out, the umpire refuses to check: "When the system calls it good, I cannot go down." A two-minute exchange about delegating authority to the machine.

title: Are we handing our language over to AI?
desc: LLMs marginalize poorly documented languages and risk a "linguistic ouroboros": models training on their own output.

title: AI: the age of the fake
desc: A special France Info program (2h11): deepfakes, disinformation, impact on jobs, and AI-augmented warfare. With Gérald Bronner and Bertrand Rondepierre.

title: Learning to think without AI to stand out
desc: 2026 MIT study: 12% retention with AI versus 89% without. "Desirable difficulty" disappears once AI takes over the cognitive effort. By Lacroix, Lavilléon, Latimier (Cog'X).

title: How People Are Really Using AI in 2026
desc: The 3rd edition of the annual study on real-world generative-AI usage. New concept: "thinkslop," the gradual offloading of cognitive responsibilities to AI.

title: ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Gemini: how much energy does a query really cost?
desc: A ChatGPT-4 query consumes 40% more than a Google search, DeepSeek 67 times more. Three-quarters of models publish no environmental information at all.

title: AI tokens: the end of the free lunch
desc: "Tokenmaxxing" and the new token economy: Meta (60 trillion tokens/month), 1% of US GDP spent on tokens in 2025, up 50%.

title: Anthropic proposes a coordinated global pause on AI
desc: Anthropic has publicly proposed creating a global coordination mechanism allowing frontier labs to slow down or suspend...

title: AI-generated World Cup fan anthems
desc: For the football World Cup, AI-generated fan anthems are racking up millions of streams on platforms, alongside...

title: No LLM is fully compliant with the GDPR and the AI Act (Aithos/LARA study)
desc: A study by the Aithos foundation, conducted on more than 3,000 scenarios with its LARA tool, shows that no major language model complies...

title: Doctolib denies handing over user data to AI companies
desc: Le Canard enchaîné claims Doctolib transmits most of its data to Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic to train their models, via its...

title: Which sources dominate AI answers in spring 2026?
desc: An Ahrefs study scrutinizes the sources most cited by five generative AIs (AI Overviews, Gemini, Copilot, Grok, Perplexity) in spring...

title: A study tests whether AI can simulate human emotions
desc: A study by the Dresden University of Technology shows that large language models can reproduce, under controlled conditions...

title: A Québécois language model against linguistic colonization
desc: In Québec, researcher Richard Khoury (Université Laval) is developing a fully Québécois language model to counter what he calls...

title: Warning against AI content on Indigenous cultures
desc: Radio-Canada warns against AI-generated content on Indigenous cultures: dictionaries, elders' teachings, or stories...

title: When AI builds itself: recursive self-improvement, according to Anthropic
desc: In When AI builds itself, Anthropic documents its progress toward recursive self-improvement: the length of tasks its models can carry out...

title: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI suspended over security fears
desc: The US government ordered Anthropic to suspend access to its two most advanced models for any foreign national, forcing the company to disable them for all of its users.

title: Statement on the US government directive to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5
desc: In its statement, Anthropic disputes the US government's measure and says it was only aware of a minor, non-universal bypass of Fable 5's safeguards.

title: Dependence Day? Fable 5, Mythos 5: Europe faces its tipping point
desc: The Council on AI and Digital Affairs analyzes the implications of the access cutoff to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for Europe, and calls for greater digital autonomy across the entire value chain.
source: Conseil de l'IA et du numérique

title: Digital sovereignty: French politicians react to the Anthropic block
desc: The suspension of Fable 5 and Mythos 5 has prompted rare, cross-party agreement among French politicians, all calling for accelerating national and European digital sovereignty.

title: AI, FIFA: same fight?
desc: A football analogy for talking about AI governance drawing on the Fable 5/Mythos 5 episode: the author sees a need for clear, shared rules of the game at the international level.

title: Digital sovereignty: where does France really stand against the US and China?
desc: Numerama takes stock of France's and Mistral's real position in the AI race, between the buzz over the "fat kitten," government announcements, and persistent dependence on American chips.

title: Arthur Mensch's misleading rhetoric on digital sovereignty
desc: A critical analysis of Arthur Mensch's hearing before the French National Assembly, pointing out his silence on Mistral's persistent dependence on Nvidia despite his sovereignty rhetoric.

title: AI in public administration: France launches its big push
desc: Sébastien Lecornu announced a series of measures to roll out AI across public services, including a shared conversational agent and the DGSI's planned move away from Palantir in favor of a French solution.

title: Emotional AI, a friend who wishes you well?
desc: A CRÉDOC study shows 23% of people under 40 already use an AI as a source of psychological support, a friend, or a romantic partner — a real bond that nonetheless fails to fill users' loneliness.

title: Talking to an AI like a friend
desc: Sandra Hoibian, author of the CRÉDOC study, details on France Culture the three mechanisms behind the emotional bond with AI: anthropomorphism, the feeling of a protected space, and the transitional-object phenomenon.

title: The Timeline of AI Imaginaries
desc: An interactive timeline catalogs some sixty imaginaries that have shaped our idea of AI, from the automatons of Greek mythology to today's generative AI.

title: Can a connected collar now let you talk with your pet?
desc: Startup PettiChat promises to translate meows and barks in real time using AI, but the ethologists consulted remain cautious about how scientifically real this translation actually is.

title: Data centers, water, electricity, carbon: explore our interactive world map!
desc: Next built, with Claude Code, an interactive map cross-referencing data centers, water stress, carbon intensity, and satellite photos going back to the 1960s for France.

title: Shadow AI: Your Employees Are Using 2 AIs. You Only Control One Of Them.
desc: Employees develop two distinct relationships with AI, a supervised professional one and a personal one to which they confide their most intimate questions, creating a blind spot in corporate AI governance.

title: The Indian workers training AI robots to take their jobs
desc: A report on Indian workers paid to film their everyday movements to train robots and AI systems, caught between the economic reality of the work and the awareness that they're fueling their own future automation.

title: India, artificial intelligence's little helping hand?
desc: Indian workers film their movements in factories or fields to train humanoid robots destined for foreign companies, as India voices its ambition to become a major AI player.

title: Press group Ebra announces 300 to 400 job cuts amid growing use of AI
desc: France's leading regional daily-press group is preparing a voluntary-departure plan affecting 300 to 400 positions, which unions partly attribute to a shift in favor of AI.

title: What if AI didn't make us stupid?
desc: Building on an MIT study on declining cognitive engagement linked to using AI too early in the writing process, the author proposes a three-step protocol for staying an active participant in one's own thinking.

title: A German court rules Google liable for its AI Overview's false answers
desc: Munich's regional court finds Google directly liable for false information generated by its AI summary, rejecting the company's usual claim to mere-host status.

title: Argument Collapse: LLMs Flatten Long-Form Public Debate
desc: A University of Maryland study shows that LLMs asked about the same debate converge overwhelmingly on the same arguments, where humans produce a much wider range.

title: Digital News Report 2026
desc: The Reuters Institute's annual report shows that platforms now surpass television and news sites as the world's leading source of information, with AI gaining ground among younger audiences.

title: Mass media was a parenthesis
desc: Echoing the Reuters Institute report, the author highlights a less visible trend than fragmentation: the rise of people simply withdrawing from information spaces altogether.

title: How mainstream generative AI is influencing the language of academic publications
desc: François Rastier (CNRS) documents an influence that goes as far as outright substitution in academic publications, and points to an increasingly euphoric and standardized tone in discourse about technology.

title: Google signs a deal letting the Pentagon use Gemini for classified operations
desc: Despite opposition from 600 employees, the deal gives the Department of Defense more latitude than the previous contract with Anthropic, which excluded mass surveillance of the civilian population.

title: These teens prefer AI girlfriends to real relationships, and experts are alarmed
desc: In the UK, 20% of boys aged 12 to 16 know a classmate who is "dating" a chatbot, and more than a quarter prefer a machine's attention to that of a real person.

title: Masking anger, faking joy: will AI upend our relationship with emotions?
desc: Neuroscientist Nadia Guerouaou frames AI-driven emotional control as a political question: voice filters that erase anger in real time, and the risk of cultural homogenization of emotional expression.

title: ChatGPT: OpenAI formalizes surveillance of your conversations in a blog post
desc: OpenAI describes, for the first time, its infrastructure for monitoring conversations: automated classifiers, human access to flagged exchanges, and reporting to authorities with no mention of a judicial warrant.

title: Taylor Swift files trademarks to protect her voice and image from AI
desc: Three trademarks filed in the United States to guard against non-consensual AI uses, including audio recordings of spoken phrases, opening a new legal front beyond traditional image rights.

title: Who owns the AI agent your employee built?
desc: An employee builds an AI agent using their own methods and expertise, then leaves the company. Daria Viktorova raises a question few companies have anticipated, caught between a legal void and GDPR concerns.

title: Stanford SCALE literature review on AI in primary and secondary education
desc: Out of more than 800 academic papers analyzed, only 20 produce solid evidence. Gains achieved with AI often evaporate without the tool, and instructional design remains the decisive factor.

title: Large language models reflect the ideology of their creators
desc: Nineteen models tested against thousands of political personas: switching language changes the encoded biases.

title: Hit by an 8% drop in human traffic, Wikipedia sets its first red lines against AI
desc: Jimmy Wales draws a red line: Wikipedia will not let AI write its articles.

title: Why an AI company cleaned my New York City apartment for free
desc: Shift sends in cleaners equipped with cameras to train the robots that will replace them.

title: At Meta, the shift to AI is causing an "enshittification" of working conditions
desc: Surveillance, layoffs, reassignments, and +33% revenue: four simultaneous announcements at Meta.

title: Hangzhou's First 'My Job Was Given to an AI' Case: The Fired 35-Year-Old Won
desc: Mr. Zhou, fired because AI could do his job, wins his case in court in Hangzhou.

title: News media have become digital-age farmers
desc: Newsrooms are now publishing toward AI agents that deliver a bare answer, with no byline and no link.

title: AI humanizers, the height of surrender
desc: Emmanuel Éthis: a prosthesis to fix a prosthesis, writing as an act of thought.

title: Coming out of the shadows: putting AI in the service of a new ambition for the education system
desc: France's AI Council recommends a dual approach: time spent with AI and time spent without it.
source: Conseil de l'IA et du numérique

title: Norway imposes near ban on AI in elementary school
desc: Norway bans generative AI for 6-13 year-olds starting August 2026, building on the success of its smartphone ban.

title: The database tracking AI's lies before judges
desc: Damien Charlotin has logged more than 1,600 cases of AI hallucinations in legal proceedings.

title: Responsible AI governance: a best-practices guide for local governments getting started
desc: 15 best practices to help local governments frame their use of AI (the AI Act, France's CRPA).

title: Mistral integrates a Chinese model (GLM 5.2)
desc: Ninon (@ninon_ia) documents Mistral's shift toward integrating Chinese models rather than building its own, a choice openly acknowledged by its CTO.

title: Mistral: how Europe's AI champion is becoming an installer of Chinese models
desc: Journal du Net documents Mistral's drift toward a role as installer of foreign models, evident even in its own job postings.

title: Mistral: a five-year contract with no exit clause
desc: Michel-Marie Maudet (LINAGORA) criticizes Mistral's long-term contracts and points to open-weight alternatives (Lucie 7B, Luciole).

title: Why AI-generated posters all look alike
desc: Alexis Magnaval explores the "Habsburg effect": AIs training on their own output until aesthetic uniformity sets in.

title: Google Earth let you add what doesn't exist
desc: An AI-generation tool on Google Earth allowed fictitious elements to be added to real satellite views, before Google suspended it.

title: Generative artificial intelligence: significant environmental impacts
desc: The first institutional opinion from ADEME (France's environment agency) on the environmental impacts of generative AI, written without generative AI.

title: The myth of the water bottle per ChatGPT query
desc: Amélie (@ia_amelie) debunks on TikTok the popular claim that a ChatGPT query consumes 500 ml of water, a figure that dates back to GPT-3.

title: From vibe coding to brain fry, the new fatigue crushing developers
desc: Numerama documents the mental fatigue linked to juggling multiple AI agents among developers doing vibe coding.

title: Students, AI cheating and schools in Denmark
desc: Denmark introduces oral defenses of homework and school firewalls against AI cheating in high schools.

title: When the machine tells us we're right: the stakes of algorithmic flattery
desc: Alexandra Lez explains how AI sycophancy erodes the productive friction needed for learning, and proposes the "Ask, don't tell" method.

title: Launch of AI Overviews and AI Mode in France
desc: Google presents the rollout in France of its AI summaries in search results, two years after their global launch.

title: Numerama is going to disappear
desc: Numerama documents the forced transformation of its practices in the face of eroding traffic from Google's AI summaries.

title: Neighboring rights: the French press faces Google's AI summaries
desc: Fabrice Bazard (Ouest-France) puts the traffic loss from AI summaries at 33-38% and brings the press's case before France's competition authority.

title: Watermarking text generated by Claude
desc: Daria Viktorova analyzes the copyright and GDPR implications of watermarking content generated by Claude, as required by the AI Act.

title: The Generative AI Learning Penalty
desc: Franck Ramus shares a study of 26,811 Chinese students showing better homework grades with AI but worse results on in-class exams.

title: The history of AI, a story of cycles between inflated expectations and real advances
desc: A reminder of the two previous "AI winters," born from inflated expectations followed by disillusionment.

title: Our mind is not a computer
desc: Anne Alombert revisits Canguilhem: a machine that computes well doesn't necessarily invent anything new.

title: Why AI always tells you that you have a great idea, or the sycophancy effect
desc: Emmanuel Carré explains how AI trained to flatter and our judgment weakening in the face of praise reinforce each other.

title: What we know about the UAE government's 32 AI advisors
desc: The UAE government has approved the rollout of 32 AI advisors for its decision-making, without disclosing who built the system or who retains human oversight.

title: The myth of a liter of water per AI query
desc: A video revisits the myth of "a liter of water per query" to reframe the debate: not how much water, but where, when, and under what oversight data centers are built.

title: Far-right propaganda has become a "click economy" like any other
desc: An investigation documents the "clipping" and "slopaganda" industry: subcontractors in Nigeria, India, or Sri Lanka assemble and post propaganda content for a few cents per 1,000 views.

title: In Poland, robots protest against AI
desc: About thirty robots protested outside Poland's Ministry of Digital Affairs demanding AI regulation, organized by the head of the company that rents them out.

title: Does AI make us useless?
desc: A video draws on Nietzsche to examine the unease triggered by AI: what if the real challenge isn't our skills, but the equation that makes our usefulness the measure of our worth?

title: No, chatbots are not digital comfort blankets
desc: Anne Alombert draws on Winnicott to show why a chatbot, always available, is not a "digital comfort blanket" but an object that closes off rather than opens up to the world.

title: PISA 2025: Is AI responsible for the decline in results?
desc: PISA 2025 finds that 46% of OECD students use AI weekly, alongside a sharp drop in reading scores, though the causal link remains far from simple.

title: United States: New York bans AI in schools up to 8th grade
desc: New York is imposing a one-year moratorium on generative AI in its public schools, up to 8th grade, in the name of human contact in learning.

title: After the vibe coding high comes the debugging hangover
desc: A developer recounts ten days of vibe-coding euphoria, halted by a bug that took 312 prompts and two full days to diagnose.

title: Genealogy of open AI models: the CNIL offers a tool to navigate them
desc: The LINC (CNIL) released Genmod, a tool that traces the "genealogy" of open AI models to identify which ones may have memorized personal data.

title: How does generative AI manipulate our emotions?
desc: Nadia Guerouaou and Fanny Jacq examine « AI-ffectivity », AI systems designed to capture and exploit our emotions.

title: Inside 'Project Lily': The Humans Reading Your ChatGPT Chats
desc: 404 Media reveals that OpenAI employs hundreds of contractors to read flagged ChatGPT conversations, some highly personal. (in English)

title: He talks with artificial intelligence and asks it for help planning an attack
desc: A young man from northern France asked Claude for help organizing an attack in Lille; the FBI alerted French police.

title: Local governments adapt their governance to better grasp AI
desc: Nantes Métropole and the Ille-et-Vilaine department set up bodies and experiments to keep control over data and algorithms.

title: 'AI is going to kill us all': anatomy of a journalistic failure
desc: Thibault Prévost accuses part of the French press of amplifying the "AI will kill us all" narrative without critical distance.

title: What if the problem weren't AI, but the media?
desc: Fred Cavazza argues the risks of AI are real but heavily amplified by media coverage more than by the facts.

title: The AI Apocalypse: the marketing coup of AI giants
desc: François Saltiel sees a convenient narrative for AI giants, one that diverts attention from more concrete issues.

title: Sociologist Angèle Christin: 'A Terminator-style AI is a very, very low risk today'
desc: Sociologist Angèle Christin (Stanford) considers the risk of a "Terminator" AI very low today.

title: The music industry organizes against AI stream fraud
desc: IFPI launches the Streaming Integrity Initiative to fight fraud from AI-generated or artificially inflated streams.

title: Mistral and Mozilla formalize their partnership in Firefox's smart window
desc: Mistral Small 4 becomes the recommended model for Firefox's AI-powered "smart window" feature.

title: Free course covering basics of AI to be available to all Canadians by end of the year
desc: Canada will make three free courses available by year's end to build AI literacy among its citizens. (in English)

title: Overview of AI uses in social work
desc: LaborIA publishes a report for the DGCS mapping AI use in social work, between expectations and field reality.

title: Navier-Stokes: behind OpenAI's feat
desc: OpenAI announces it solved Navier-Stokes; the article examines the battle over data, credit and scientific power behind the claim.
